bugs.title: Quick-select buttons inject comma decimal separator into amount input
bugs.description: Clicking the 10¢, 50¢ or $1 quick-select buttons sets the internal DOM value with a comma (0,50) instead of a period (0.50). The UI appears to work but the raw DOM value is technically invalid for a type=number input, which could cause issues in some browsers or with form validation.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Click the "50¢" quick-select button in the order panel
3. Open browser DevTools and inspect the value attribute of the #orderSize input
bugs.expected: value="0.50" (period decimal separator, valid for type=number)
bugs.actual: value="0,50" (comma decimal separator — invalid for type=number inputs)

bugs.human_review_reason: The screenshot shows the amount input displaying '0,10' with a comma decimal separator, which visually supports the core claim that the input uses commas instead of periods. However, the bug report specifically describes clicking '50¢' to reproduce, while the screenshot shows '0,10' (10¢ selected), so the exact reproduction step shown differs from what's described.
bugs.screenshot_comment: The amount input field visibly displays '0,10' with a comma decimal separator, directly corroborating the reported behavior. The 10¢ quick-select button appears active/selected, and the comma separator is clearly visible in the input.

bugs.title: aria-valuemin attribute has float precision artifact (root cause of BUG-006)
bugs.description: The #orderSize input has aria-valuemin set to 0.10000000149011612 instead of 0.10. This floating-point artifact causes the browser validation to incorrectly reject orders for exactly $0.10 (the stated minimum), because 0.10 < 0.10000000149011612.
bugs.expected: aria-valuemin="0.10" (exact decimal matching the stated minimum)

bugs.title: Shares preview rounds to 1 decimal place instead of 2 (overstates share count)
bugs.description: The order panel shows a shares preview that rounds to 1 decimal place. This causes the displayed share count to be higher than what the user will actually receive. For example at $0.50 with avg price 66¢ the correct result is 0.76 shares but the UI shows 0.8. At $0.10 the overstatement is 33%.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Select Blue Team in the order panel
bugs.expected: $0.50 ÷ $0.66 = 0.757 → displayed as 0.76 shares (rounded to 2 decimal places)
bugs.actual: UI displays 0.8 shares (rounded to 1 decimal place — 5% overstatement)

bugs.title: Epoch History — Performance column values not selectable or readable by screen readers
bugs.description: In the Epoch History table, the Performance column shows percentage values visually but they are rendered purely via CSS (::before/::after pseudo-elements). The actual text is not in the HTML — so users cannot select/copy the values, screen readers cannot read them, and automated tests cannot access them.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Scroll down to the Epoch History table
3. Try to select/highlight a value in the Performance column
4. Open DevTools and inspect a Performance column cell
bugs.expected: Performance percentage values are real text in the HTML, selectable and readable by screen readers
bugs.actual: Performance column cells are empty in the HTML — values appear only as CSS pseudo-elements and cannot be selected, copied, or read by assistive technology

bugs.title: Probability chart Y-axis goes above 100% (mathematically impossible)
bugs.description: The probability chart Y-axis shows values up to 120%, which is impossible for a probability scale (max is always 100%). The chart does not enforce a 0–100% domain constraint.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Scroll to the Price Chart section
3. Look at the Y-axis labels on the probability chart
bugs.actual: Y-axis shows 120% at the top of the scale

bugs.title: Order for exactly $0.10 (stated minimum) is falsely rejected
bugs.description: Placing an order for exactly $0.10 — the advertised minimum — triggers an error saying the amount is below minimum. The error message is self-contradictory: "Order cost $0.10 below minimum $0.10". Root cause is BUG-002: the float precision artifact in aria-valuemin causes 0.10 to be evaluated as less than 0.10000000149011612.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Click the "10¢" quick-select button in the order panel
bugs.expected: Order for $0.10 is accepted (it equals the stated minimum)
bugs.actual: Error shown: "Order cost $0.10 below minimum $0.10" — order is rejected even though amount equals the minimum

bugs.title: "Resting order placed" message stays visible after the order is cancelled
bugs.description: After cancelling a resting (limit) order, the confirmation message "Resting order placed — BLUE @ $X" remains visible in the order panel. The order is gone ("Cancelled 1 order(s)" toast confirms it) but the panel still implies an active resting order exists.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Set an amount and place a resting order (price below current market)
3. Observe the "Resting order placed — BLUE @ $X" confirmation message in the order panel
4. Find the order in the My Open Orders table and cancel it
5. Wait 3+ seconds and look at the order panel
bugs.expected: Confirmation message clears or updates after the order is cancelled
bugs.actual: "Resting order placed — BLUE @ $0.6644" message stays in the order panel even though the order no longer exists

bugs.title: Blue Team orderbook tab sometimes shows Red Team prices
bugs.description: When the Blue Team tab is selected in the Orderbook section, the prices displayed are in the Red Team range ($0.33–$0.39) instead of the Blue Team range (~$0.61–$0.67). Switching tabs back and forth did not resolve it during testing. This could cause users to make trading decisions based on wrong prices.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Scroll to the Orderbook section and expand it
4. Observe the prices listed in the orderbook
bugs.expected: Blue Team tab shows prices in the Blue Team range (~$0.61–$0.67)
bugs.actual: Blue Team tab shows prices in the Red Team range ($0.33–$0.39)

bugs.title: Orderbook Shares and Total column values not selectable or readable by screen readers
bugs.description: In the Orderbook table, the Shares and Total columns show values visually but the HTML cells are empty — values are rendered via CSS only. Same issue as BUG-004 in the Epoch History table. Values cannot be selected, copied, or read by screen readers or automated tests.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Scroll to the Orderbook section and expand it
3. Try to select/highlight a value in the Shares or Total column
4. Open DevTools and inspect a cell in those columns
bugs.expected: Shares and Total values are real text in the HTML, selectable and readable
bugs.actual: Column cells are empty <span> elements in HTML — values appear only via CSS and cannot be selected or read by assistive technology

bugs.title: Epoch volume shown as $0 in status bar but $1 in probability bar simultaneously
bugs.description: Two parts of the UI show different values for the same epoch volume at the same time. The epoch status bar (top strip) shows "VOLUME $0" while the probability bar section shows "$1 vol". One of the values must be wrong. May be a race condition or delayed update.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Look at the epoch status bar at the top — note the VOLUME value
3. Look at the probability bar section — note the vol value
bugs.expected: Both the epoch status bar and the probability bar show the same volume for the current epoch
bugs.actual: Epoch status bar shows "VOLUME $0" while probability bar shows "$1 vol" at the same moment

bugs.title: Typing a negative amount shows negative shares preview (e.g. "-1.5 shares")
bugs.description: When a negative number is typed into the amount input, the shares preview calculates and displays a negative share count instead of showing 0 or an error state. The validation message does appear correctly but the live preview underneath it is still misleading.
steps_to_reproduce: 2. Click the amount input in the order panel
4. Observe the Shares preview value below the input
bugs.expected: Shares preview shows 0 or a blank/error state for invalid negative input
bugs.actual: Shares preview shows "-1.5" — a nonsensical negative number

bugs.title: Submit button loses team name on negative input but keeps it on above-max input
bugs.description: The submit button label behaves inconsistently for two types of invalid input. With a negative amount the button shows just "Buy" (team name disappears). With an above-maximum amount the button correctly shows "Buy Blue Team". Both are invalid inputs — the button should behave the same way for both.
steps_to_reproduce: 4. Clear the input and type "1000001" (above maximum)
5. Observe the submit button label again and compare
bugs.expected: Submit button consistently shows the team name ("Buy Blue Team" or "Buy Red Team") regardless of whether input is invalid
bugs.actual: Negative input ("-1"): button shows "Buy" — team name is lost. Above-max input ("1000001"): button correctly shows "Buy Blue Team". Inconsistent.
